To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the TSPA for the repository at Yuccamontan, Nevada, has been successfully performed using Latin hypercube sampling to generate a mapping of uncertain inputs to analysis outputs of interest; (2) the resultant mapping is useful for uncertainty and sensitivity analysis, and (3) the resultant mapping can provide useful insights about analysis results.
the TSPA results are sensitive to a large number of epistemically uncertain input parameters and that the TSPA is relatively insensitive to the uncertainty in the epistemically uncertain parameters.

the uncertainty in releases from the unsaturated zone is dominated by the uncertainty in the solubility of the most soluble radionuclide, the uncertainty in releases through the saturated zone is dominated by a combination of uncertainty in the solute transport parameters, and uncertainty in annual dose to the REEI from the most soluble radiumuclides is dominated by a number of factors including solute transport parameters and solubility.
In summary, our research is concerned with

(i) the use of Latin hypercube sampling for generating distributions for epistemically uncertain input parameters, (ii) the use of scatterplots to explore relationships between epistemically and aleatoric uncertain input parameters and analysis outcomes, and (iii) the use of partial rank correlation coefficients for quantifying the relative importance of input parameters on output variables.
the development and application of uncertainty and sensitivity analysis techniques for TSPA analyses.
the application of uncertainty and sensitivity analysis to TSPA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the uncertainty and sensitivity analyses performed to date for Yucca Mountain 2008 Performance Assessment have yielded useful results and have contributed to the credibility of the analysis.

the uncertainty analysis and sensitivity analysis procedures used in the TSPA for the proposed high-level radioactive waste repository at the Yucca Mountain site are well-founded, and that the results are credible and informative.

the results from uncertainty and sensitivity analyses for physical processes in the TSPA are consistent with the results from uncertainty analyses for physical processes performed previously in the TSPA and with results obtained in other performance assessments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
uncertainty and sensitivity analyses are a valuable tool for understanding and assessing analysis results.
the results are consistent with the overall TSPA results.

uncertainty analysis results indicate that analysis outcomes are uncertain and sensitivity analysis results show that analysis outcomes are highly sensitive to epistemically uncertain input distributions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the TSPA, uncertainty in releases is primarily driven by uncertainty in solubility, while uncertainty in dose to the RMI is primarily driven by uncertainties in solubility and retardation.
the uncertainty and sensitivity analysis for TSPA is a complex and challenging task.
uncertainty in analysis outcomes is dominated by uncertainty in the unsaturated zone (e.g., 90% of uncertainty in annual dose to the RMED is due to unsaturated zone uncertainty).
